response.text: Bakery is no longer part of the primary fresh workstream [1, 2]. Originally included alongside produce, dairy, and chilled ready meals [3], bakery was descoped during the November 17, 2025 go/no-go decision after UAT revealed poor forecasting accuracy, largely because roughly half to sixty percent of bakery items are baked in-store rather than being a pure ordering issue [4, 5, 6]. Consequently, the fresh go-live proceeded solely with produce, dairy, and chilled ready meals, while bakery was established as its own separate workstream [2, 6, 7]. Under this standalone workstream, bakery is being implemented with partner Meridian, with the boundary structured so that the system generates a store-, article-, and day-level demand signal/forecast while Meridian manages the production plan [8, 9, 10].

results.question: Is bakery part of the fresh workstream now? How did its scope change?

response.text:
No, bakery is no longer part of the primary fresh workstream [1, 2]. 

Its scope evolved through the following stages:
- **Initial inclusion**: Bakery was originally one of the four core fresh categories alongside produce, dairy, and chilled ready meals [3, 4].
- **Descoping from Fresh Phase 2**: In the November 17, 2025 go/no-go meeting, bakery accuracy was identified as poor because roughly half to sixty percent of the category is baked in-store rather than a standard ordering problem [5, 6, 7]. It was decided to descope bakery from the December fresh go-live (which proceeded with produce, dairy, and chilled ready meals) [1, 8, 9].
- **Establishment as a separate workstream**: Bakery was shifted into its own standalone workstream [1, 10]. In this revised scope, implemented in collaboration with partner Meridian, Meridian owns the production plan while RELEX provides the store, article, and daily demand forecast signal [11, 12, 13].

response.text:
No — bakery is not part of the fresh workstream now. It is out of scope for fresh: "Yes for produce, so dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery Bakery is out of scope." [1] and "Bakery descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026." [2]

Initially fresh included "so Produce, dairy, bakery, the chilled ready meals. Sofia would give you a better answer." [3] A proposal was to stage delivery as "Rather than delivering all four fresh categories together in one go-live, we would" [4] "deliver produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery. Three smaller" [5] "go-lives roughly six weeks apart." [6]

That three-wave proposal was not approved. What was approved is "What was actually decided on Monday is two deliveries, not three: produce, dairy and" [7] "chilled ready meals together in December, and bakery separately as its own workstream." [8] The go/no-go decision was "Then that is my decision. Go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery comes later as its own," [9] and the record states "This is two deliveries rather than three. Any plan document showing three waves is superseded." [10]

The reason given was "Bakery is poor because half of it is baked in store and it is not" [11] "really an ordering problem." [12] Later quantified as "About sixty percent bakery is baked in store. That is not an ordering decision," [13]

Present scope is separate from fresh: "Bakery workstream scoping with Meridian has begun." [14] with "Bakery build progressing." [15] described as "in in build with Meridian." [16] where "bakery. Meridian owns the production plan, we own the demand signal, and today we agree where," [17]

response.text: Bakery is not part of the Fresh Phase 2 go-live scope now; it is a separate bakery workstream. The current fresh go-live scope is produce, dairy and chilled ready meals [8][9]. Bakery was descoped to its own workstream starting March 2026 [9], and the steering report says this is two deliveries rather than three, with any three-wave plan superseded [10]. The change: the kickoff listed produce, dairy, bakery and chilled ready meals together [1]; a proposal suggested three waves—produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery [2][3]; but the actual decision was two deliveries, not three: produce, dairy and chilled ready meals together in December, and bakery separately as its own workstream [4][5]. At the 17 Nov go/no-go, the decision was to go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals, with bakery later as its own [6], and bakery was recorded as descoped to a separate workstream [7]. The December cutover call confirmed bakery is out of scope [8]. The descope was discussed because bakery accuracy was poor and half of bakery is baked in store, not an ordering problem [17][18][19]. Bakery scoping/design with Meridian followed [11][12]. By the Q2 business review, next steps were chain-wide rollout for the three fresh categories and bakery in build with Meridian [13][14]; bakery build is progressing [15].

The December cutover call confirmed bakery is out of scope.
The steering report says bakery was descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026, and this is two deliveries rather than three, with any plan document showing three waves superseded.
The descope was discussed because bakery accuracy was poor and half of bakery is baked in store, not an ordering problem.
Bakery came out of the December go-live; bakery workstream scoping with Meridian began, and a bakery design workshop followed.
By the Q2 business review, next steps were chain-wide rollout for the three fresh categories and bakery in build with Meridian; bakery build is progressing.

results.question: Is bakery part of the fresh workstream now? How did its scope change?

stages.raw_response: {"action":"question","needsEvidence":true,"research":"chronology"}

response.text:
No — bakery is not part of the current Fresh Phase 2 go-live/three fresh categories. The approved/current scope is produce, dairy and chilled ready meals, with bakery descoped to a separate workstream [1][2][3][4][5]. The Q2 2026 review describes two next-step conversations: chain-wide rollout for the three fresh categories, and bakery in build with Meridian [4][5]. The steering report confirms bakery was descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026 and that any three-wave plan is superseded [2][3].

Scope change: The 2024 kickoff listed produce, dairy, bakery and chilled ready meals [6]. A sequencing proposal suggested three waves: produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery [7][8][9]. But the recorded decision was two deliveries: produce, dairy and chilled ready meals together in December, and bakery separately as its own workstream [10][11]. At the 17 Nov 2025 go/no-go, bakery accuracy was poor [12], Sofia said half of bakery is baked in store and not really an ordering problem [13][14], and she said 'Then take bakery out.' [15]; Marco said 'We can descope bakery from this...' [16]. Lena decided: 'Go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery comes later as its own,' [17]. At the December cutover, bakery was out of scope [18]. Later, bakery scoping with Meridian began [19], and the bakery design workshop framed Meridian as owning the production plan while RELEX owns the demand signal [20][21]. By Q2 2026, bakery was in build with Meridian [5].

results.question: Is bakery part of the fresh workstream now? How did its scope change?

stages.raw_response: {"action":"question","needsEvidence":true,"research":"chronology"}

response.text:
No — bakery is not part of the fresh workstream now. It was descoped at the 17 Nov 2025 go/no-go and now runs as its own separate workstream, in build with Meridian.

Scope change: In the earlier phase-2 sequencing proposal, all four fresh categories were to be delivered in three waves — produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery [1][2]. At the 17 Nov 2025 go/no-go, Lena Fischer decided: "Go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery comes later as its own" workstream [3], and bakery was recorded as "descoped to a separate" workstream [4]. The steering report confirms "Bakery descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026" and that this is two deliveries rather than three, superseding any three-wave plan [5][6]. At the 11 Dec 2025 cutover call, bakery was confirmed "out of scope" [7]. Bakery workstream scoping with Meridian began [8], with a scoping meeting on 2026-01-28 [9] and a design workshop on 2026-03-17 [10]. At the Q2 2026 business review, the two tracks were "chain wide rollout for the three fresh categories, and bakery" which is "in build with Meridian" [11][12].

Reason: bakery accuracy was poor because about half/sixty percent is baked in store and is not really an ordering problem [13][14].
